names: Diphosphates (i) Disodium diphosphate (ii) Trisodium diphosphate (iii) Tetrasodium diphosphate (iv) Dipotassium diphosphate (v) Tetrapotassium diphosphate (vi) Dicalcium diphosphate (vii) Calcium dihydrogen diphosphate

more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
Approved in the US.
US food use is subject to the listed CFR provisions and their conditions, checked in 2026.
No current country-wide food-use ban was confirmed in the regulatory sources checked in 2026.
The permissions checked in 2026 apply only to the specified preparations, food uses and conditions.
more_info.overview: Diphosphates are salts containing two linked phosphate units; E450 includes several sodium, potassium and calcium forms. Its emulsifying role is to help form or maintain mixtures of oil and water in the finished food. One specified form is supplied as white powder. EU permissions include bread and rolls, processed fish and fishery products including molluscs and crustaceans.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; water, including natural mineral water as defined in Directive 2009/54/EC and spring water and all other bottled or packed waters; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products; unripened cheese excluding products falling in category 16.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.daily_intake: 40 mg phosphorus/kg body weight/day, combined phosphates (EFSA, 2019).
more_info.side_effects:
Estimated combined exposure exceeded the limit in some groups.
Animal evidence supports low acute toxicity.
